body.title: Qualify and prove an early live block checkpoint
body.summary: Separate availability/kill switch from default routing, admit explicit qualified pilots, and version the changed compact adapter boundary. Reuse installed qualification collection/replay and current authorization checks. Deploy the reviewed build to the daemon and obtain one actual Claude/source-only durable block ACK on an exact existing canonical subject before continuing downstream work.
acceptanceChecks: A reviewed explicit manifest covers CLI/runtime images, adapter/catalog/final schema, resolved launch/config permissions, broker/binding/auth/isolation code and security-relevant dependencies; unknown closure fails closed. Boundary changes invalidate proof; unrelated report changes do not bypass current deterministic authorization checks.

Capture fresh installed compact-boundary qualification with actual inventory and active instruction/plugin/hook canaries. Old v2 proof is retained as historical, never relabelled; Codex/indexed mode are not inferred qualified.

Explicit pilot requires normal user-authorized execution plus availability, valid exact scope and qualification, while default remains legacy. Default activation cannot be granted by caller booleans or fixture labels.

Run serial installed-Claude/source-only pilot against the same deployed boundary using already provable canonical scope and TESTS identity; record actual read and durable block receipt, run/source/boundary IDs and actual or unavailable consumption. A mock ACK or CLI exit is insufficient.

If installation/restart is required, stop at that concrete operational prerequisite and resume this pilot after daemon update. If pilot fails, preserve the same run/diagnostics and fix the failing slice; do not mark Task passed or continue t3 without a real ACK.

Early pilot uses a separately complete canonical subject with an existing approved ISSUE scope and valid TESTS repo/history identity, independent of t3's new BUILD manifest and writer corrections. It proves compact execution/progress, not the later writer changes.
